title: Macd
caption:
MACD looks complicated. It's really just two moving averages talking to each other.

It's the gap between a fast and a slow average. The signal line smooths it out: crossing above means momentum is turning up, below means it's turning down. Shrinking histogram bars mean momentum is fading.

Like any average, it lags, and it chops in sideways markets.

MACD is one of the Pro indicators on Meme Street. Practise at memestreet.net

narration: MACD looks complicated. It's really just two moving averages talking to each other. MACD is the gap between a fast and a slow moving average, usually the twelve and twenty six period EMA. When the fast one pulls away, the gap grows. The signal line is a smoothed version of MACD. When MACD crosses above it, momentum is turning up. When it crosses below, momentum is turning down. The histogram shows the distance between the two. Shrinking bars mean the momentum is fading. Like any moving average, it lags. And in choppy, sideways markets, it gives lots of false crosses. MACD is one of the Pro indicators on Meme Street. Practise reading it at memestreet.net.
